title: Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment Bill 2013
short_title: Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment Bill 2013

speeches.speaker: Peter Dutton
speeches.brief: Introduced a bill simplifying how the government's private health insurance rebate is indexed, replacing a complex per-policy system industry said would cost more than $15 million to implement across over 34,000 policies, with the new single adjustment factor expected to cut those administrative costs by around 80 per cent.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Southcott
speeches.brief: Supported the Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, noting that 10.6 million Australians hold private health insurance including 76.3 per cent of voters in the Boothby electorate, and defended premium increases needed after an 8 per cent rise in benefits paid to fund members in 2013.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Laming
speeches.brief: Defended the 30 per cent private health insurance rebate, arguing it draws Australians who would otherwise use public hospitals into private cover and funds private hospital infrastructure, noting 10 per cent of privately insured Australians earn less than $25,000 a year and citing 47 per cent hospital cover and 55 per cent general cover nationally.

speeches.speaker: Nick Champion
speeches.brief: Argued that the private health insurance rebate has little effect on coverage rates, noting more than 105,000 people took out cover between June and September last year, and defended Labor's means-testing of the rebate as delivering $700 million in savings that helped fund regional cancer centres like the one at Clare Hospital.

speeches.speaker: Natasha Griggs
speeches.brief: Supported streamlining private health insurance rebate calculations, saying the change will cut about 80 per cent of administrative costs, and reported that around 50 per cent of the Northern Territory's population, or 99,983 people, has private health cover, while welcoming the government's $110 million contribution, plus $40 million from the Country Liberal government, toward a new $150 million Palmerston hospital.

speeches.speaker: Amanda Rishworth
speeches.brief: Supported the bill's approximately $700 million in savings from indexing the private health insurance rebate, opposed a proposed $6 GP copayment, and accused the government of paying a consultant $2,000 a day to prepare the public for selling Medibank Private while rubber-stamping the largest private health insurance premium increase in a decade just before Christmas.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Giles
speeches.brief: Supported the shadow minister's amendment to the private health insurance bill demanding the government show how it improves competition and consumer protection, marked Medicare's 30th anniversary, and criticised the government's 23 December announcement of the largest private health insurance premium increase in a decade.

speeches.speaker: Peter Dutton
speeches.brief: Closed debate on the Private Health Insurance Legislation Amendment Bill, explaining it creates a single rebate adjustment factor applied uniformly each 1 April, accused Labor of repeatedly attacking private health insurance affecting almost 11 million Australians, and rejected the shadow minister's amendment.
